descript.abstract: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) has compiled a geodatabase containing mineral-related geospatial data for 10 countries of interest in Southwest Asia (area of study): Afghanistan, Cambodia, Laos, India, Indonesia, Iran, Nepal, North Korea, Pakistan, and Thailand. The data can be used in analyses of the extractive fuel and nonfuel mineral industries and related economic and physical infrastructure integral for the successful operation of the mineral industries within the area of study as well as the movement of mineral products across domestic and global markets. This geodatabase reflects the USGS ongoing commitment to its mission of understanding the nature and distribution of global mineral commodity supply chains by updating and publishing the georeferenced locations of mineral commodity production and processing facilities, mineral exploration and development sites, and mineral commodity exporting ports for the countries in the area of study. The geodatabase contains data feature classes from USGS, foreign governmental, and open-source sources as follows: (1) mineral production and processing facilities, (2) mineral exploration and development sites, (3) mineral occurrence sites and deposits, (4) undiscovered mineral resource tracts for copper, phosphate, and potash, (5) coal occurrence areas, (6) electric power generating facilities, (7) electric power transmission lines, (8) liquefied natural gas terminals, (9) undiscovered, technically recoverable conventional and continuous hydrocarbon resources (by USGS geologic province), (10) cumulative production and recoverable conventional resources (by oil- and gas-producing nation), and (11) major mineral exporting maritime ports.
descript.purpose: The primary goal of this project was to compile a range of geospatial data feature classes in this ArcGIS (ESRI) geodatabase that can be used in analyses of the extractive fuel and nonfuel mineral industries and the related economic and physical infrastructure of select countries in our area of study in Southwest Asia, which are integral for the successful operation of the mineral industries within the region and the transportation of mineral products across domestic and global markets.

However, as many feature classes are directly from authoritative sources or from previously published governmental or scientific work, not all layers were subjected to a new logical accuracy test. Visual comparison of the feature classes supports the robustness of the overall data for feature classes not created by the National Minerals Information Center or from other programs within the U.S. Geological Survey.

procstep.procdesc: Surveys of relevant foreign governmental mining and petroleum agencies, ministries, and scientific counterpart agencies were conducted to assess their geospatial data holdings. Three data feature classes were created by NMIC researchers using NMIC / USGS data as well as extensive research into individual operations: mineral extraction and processing facilities, mineral exploration sites, and mineral commodity exporting ports of the region. In addition, three data feature classes were created by NMIC researchers using regional- and/or country-level NMIC / USGS data: oil and gas undiscovered conventional resources (by geologic province), oil and gas undiscovered continuous resources (by geologic province), and oil and gas recoverable resources and cumulative production (by country). Data were assembled into geodatabase-normalized formats for use within the GIS and geospatial PDF map product. Additional geospatial data, such as tracts of undiscovered mineral resource assessments, land transportation and energy infrastructure, cartographic elements (rivers, lakes), and political / administrative boundaries were imported from external sources in geodatabase-normalized formats with some modifications as outlined in the database-level metadata files for each feature class. These modifications included re-labeling feature attributes to fit our GIS attributes table schema, excluding data not relevant for the purpose of the GIS product (e.g. features outside the area of interest), or merging features for ease of displaying them in the final GIS and geospatial PDF map product.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the location of 1,968 fuel and non-fuel mineral mineral processing plants Southwest Asian nations defined as Afghanistan, Cambodia, Laos, India, Indonesia, Iran, Nepal, North Korea, Pakistan, and Thailand compiled from a variety of sources by the U.S. Geological Survey’s (USGS) National Minerals Information Center. The dataset provides some generalized information about each mineral operation, such as name of the operation or facility, mineral commodity(ies) produced or processed, status (as of 2018), capacity, operator/ownership, and location descriptions. Non-GIS data were derived from Table 2 of individual country chapters published in the USGS 2018 Minerals Yearbook, Vol. III (Area Reports: International) publication. All data were reorganized and restructured from their original format to fit our GIS attributes table format, updated for accuracy when additional information was available, and georeferenced for this geodatabase using various sources that included company documents (annual reports, press releases, etc.), scientific/geologic reports, industry reports, government reports, maps, digital mapping services, and minerals- and mining-specific databases, as noted for each record. The data are intended to highlight the state of the minerals industries in select countries of Southwest Asia as of 2018.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the location of selected mineral deposits in Afghanistan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Laos, Nepal, North Korea, Pakistan, and Thailand published by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) in Open-File Report 2005-1294 and its accompanying Data Release (“Reviews of the Geology and Nonfuel Mineral Deposits of the World") [accessed at https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/2005/1294/] as well as other deposits contained in the USGS Mineral Resources Online Spatial Data [accessed at https://mrdata.usgs.gov/general/map-global.html]. The data are intended to show the general distribution of deposits in select countries of Southwest Asia for minerals that are considered major or critical to the economy and security of the United States as of 2019. This dataset provides some generalized information about each deposit, such as feature name, deposit type, mineral commodity(ies), and location descriptions. In this feature class, some entries that were inconsistent with other USGS datasets (e.g. unpublished USGS World Minerals Exploration Dataset) or duplicates across different sources were either omitted or updated if additional information was available. In addition, the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the approximate location of 318 mineral exploration sites in Afghanistan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Laos, Nepal, North Korea, Pakistan, and Thailand compiled from a variety of sources by the U.S. Geological Survey’s National Minerals Information Center in its unpublished World Minerals Exploration Database (WMED). Sources include company reports and press releases, scientific/geologic reports, industry reports, and government reports. The data are not comprehensive and are intended to highlight the general distribution of mineral exploration sites and potential areas of future mineral resource extraction and development in Africa. The dataset provides some generalized information about each exploration project, such as project name, main mineral commodity(ies) of interest, exploration status, and location descriptions if available. Note that the accuracy of locations is highly variable due to the lack of detailed information for many exploration projects. For instances in which little information beyond the name, commodity, and generalized location of an exploration site is known or available, we assigned the centroid coordinates (low accuracy) of either the first level administrative region (ADM1, if available) or the country in which the site is known to be located.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class includes polygons that represent permissive tracts for phosphate deposits of Afghanistan, India, Iran, and Pakistan. Within the study area, a handful of known occurrences and reports indicate the presence of phosphate in Permian, Cretaceous, and Paleogene sediments and in carbonatite. With the exception of the Khanneshin Carbonatite, very little is known about these occurrences. Economic or sub economic phosphate is known to occur in Neoproterozoic-Cambrian, Devonian, and Paleogene marine sediments, as well as Cambrian, Devonian, and Paleogene sediments. Additional occurrences have been identified in Ordovician, Permian, Triassic, Jurassic, and Miocene sediments, as well as in association with alkaline igneous rocks, mafic-ultramafic rocks, and volcanic rocks. In addition to phosphate deposits and occurrences associated with carbonatites, phosphate is mined from a Kiruna-type Fe-apatite deposit at Esfordi in Iran. Although the possibility of economic phosphate deposits exist, the need for detailed exploration for phosphate, the remoteness of some locations, and the probability that a deposit would not be exposed at the surface mean that one or more deposits are not likely to be identified in the near future. Even if a phosphate-bearing deposit is identified within the study area, it is not clear if the probable size, thickness, and grade ranges would allow economic development of the hypothesized resource.

enttyp.enttypd: Feature class containing information on potash geology in the form of polygons that represent permissive tracts for evaporite-related potash-bearing stratabound salt and potash-bearing halokinetic salt deposits in Afghanistan, India, Iran, Laos, Pakistan, and Thailand. Potash, as used in this report, refers to potassium-bearing minerals, ores, and processed products. Glauconite and alunite deposits as sources of potash were not considered during the assessment. The permissive tracts represent either the areal extent of, or surface projection of rocks within the upper 3 km of the Earth’s crust where undiscovered deposits of potash may be present. The dataset was created for the U.S. Geological Survey Global Mineral Resource Assessment Project (GMRAP), and published by its original authors as USGS Scientific Investigations Series Report 2010-5090-S. The primary objectives of the project were to outline the principal areas that have potential for selected undiscovered mineral resources and to estimate the probable amounts of those mineral resources to a depth of 1-3 kilometers below the earth's surface. In this feature class, all polygons that delineate permissive tracts outside of the Southwest Asia study area were excluded, some attributes were excluded or summarized, and the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

Data are stored as polygon attributes, summarized by USGS geologic province* as hydrocarbon resources in oil fields, in gas fields, and total including a BOE [barrel of oil equivalent = oil + NGL + gas (BCF/6) ]. Links to the corresponding provinces in the USGS World Energy website, which lists USGS publications for that province, are included for each record in this dataset. Data are rounded to no more than three significant digits and may not add to totals shown. Units are million barrels of oil (MMBO), billion cubic feet gas (BCFG), millions of barrels of natural gas liquids (MMBNGL), millions of barrels of liquids (MMBL), and millions of barrels of oil equivalent (MMBOE).*The names of USGS geologic provinces "Khorat Platform" and "Thailand Mesozoic Basin Belt" have been updated to "Khorat Plateau" and "Thai Cenozoic Basins" respectively in this dataset, as denoted in the "Province Notes (MemoOther)" field in the attributes table.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the power-generating stations that were operational, in rehabilitation, or had idle capacity in Afghanistan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Laos, Nepal, North Korea, Pakistan, and, Thailand in 2019. Power stations were categorized by the USGS into “Capacity Classification” groups according to their installed capacity (in megawatts, if known) and “Fuel Classifications” based on the type of fuel(s) consumed in the generation of electricity. Fuel classifications include Renewable (solar, wind, hydro, biomass, and geothermal), Non-Renewable (diesel, fuel oils including crude and heavy fuel oil, and natural gas), Hybrid (a combination of renewable and non-renewable fuel types), and Other/Unknown for those features where facility data is insufficient for categorization. In this feature class, the attribute field names have been modified from their original source to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the power transmission lines that were completed (excludes planned and under-construction) and online in Afghanistan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Laos, Nepal, North Korea, Pakistan, and Thailand in 2019. For some countries where limited data were available, this feature class may only include the major or highest voltage power transmission lines in the country. Transmission lines were categorized by the USGS into “Voltage Classification” groups according to their transmission voltages (in kilovolts). The groups are based on the classifications generally used in the global energy industry (e.g. U.S. Department of Energy, 2015, United States Electricity Industry Primer, Fig. 15; https://www.energy.gov/sites/prod/files/2015/12/f28/united-states-electricity-industry-primer.pdf): Low Voltage (LV) = <33 kV; Medium Voltage (MV) = 33-110 kV; High Voltage (HV) = 115-275 kV; and Extra High Voltage (EHV) = >275 kV. The additional classification of Ultra High Voltage (UHV) exists for transmission lines >765 kV, but as of 2019 no UHV transmission lines had been built in the area of study. In several instances, lines can transmit a range of voltages that fall into more than one classification (e.g. 110/123/150 kV lines). In those instances, lines are classified based on the highest voltage levels (e.g. 33/66/115 kV = HV).

enttyp.enttypd: This feature class contains the location of 220 fuel and non-fuel mineral commodity exporting ports in Afghanistan, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Iran, North Korea, Pakistan, and Thailand, including dry ports and oil and gas terminals, compiled from a variety of sources by the U.S. Geological Survey’s National Minerals Information Center. The dataset provides some generalized information about each port, or terminal operations within a port, such as name of the port or terminal, mineral commodity(ies) exported, exporting capacity, source and(or) destination of commodities, and operator/ownership, if available. Sources of information used to compile this dataset include the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency's World Port Index (WPI) report, U.S. Energy Information Administration country profiles, Asia maps, digital global mapping services, company and port authority reports and websites, company press releases, global industry reports, and government reports. The data are not comprehensive and are intended to highlight the general distribution of mineral commodity exporting ports in countries of Southwest Asia and their connectivity to other transportation infrastructure across Southwest Asia. In this feature class, the attribute field names have been modified from their original source(s) to fit our GIS attributes table schema; descriptive field aliases were created from the original field names in the source data.
